_about: PZB01G only. The source uses an en dash as a sentence connective ('Own –
outright', 'Neither – I live rent-free with...'), which reads as a fragment
in a persona. Rewritten as plain statements; every distinction the source
draws is preserved, including the three landlord types and the two
living-with-family cases, which differ by whether rent is paid.
This is the field that exposed the mojibake bug: 5,256 of 5,333 rows carried
a raw control byte here, because the en dash had been decoded as latin1
rather than cp1252. Fixed in sources/spss.py; see tests/test_encoding.py.
NOTHING IS COLLAPSED HERE, deliberately. There is one scheme, so there is no
second vocabulary to reconcile against and no pressure to coarsen. Rolling the
denominations up to the ONS religion groups, or the tenures up to own/rent,
would destroy detail nobody has asked us to lose in exchange for a comparability
that does not yet have a second party. When UKHLS arrives with its own variables
— and it will, SN 6849 carries both — that is the moment to decide the canonical,
with both schemes in view. Designing it now from one scheme risks exactly the
one-way-street problem in persona/categories.py: a canonical fixed too early

canonical.Lives with family or friends, paying ren: Lives with family or friends, paying rent
canonical.Lives with family or friends, rent free: Lives with family or friends, rent free

uk_yougov_tenure.Neither \u2013 I live rent-free with my: Lives with family or friends, rent free
uk_yougov_tenure.Neither \u2013 I live with my parents, f: Lives with family or friends, paying rent
